newsitem.title: INDIA: Ten die in police firing on India mob.
newsitem.headline: Ten die in police firing on India mob.

text.p: Ten people including a 12-year old girl were killed when police opened fire on an unruly mob, angered by the desecration of a statue of a prominent social activist, in India's business capital on Friday, hospital sources said.
"Eight people were already dead when they were brought in," a doctor at a city hospital told Reuters. "Two more succumbed to their injuries."
Police said earlier that four died in the incident but were unable to confirm the latest report.
All the victims had died of bullet wounds, they said.
The Press Trust of India (PTI) news agency said 11 people died in police fire.
A 12-year old girl was among those killed, the hospital sources said.
Police said they rushed a large force of special riot police to Ghatkopar, 15 km (10 miles) from the city centre, and the situation was tense but under control.
The trouble began after a statue of Bhimrao Ambedkar, a leader of the lower social classes, was found garlanded with shoes, which is viewed as a insulting gesture, police said.
When police reached the scene at 6.30 a.m. (0100 GMT) a crowd of Ambedkar supporters which had already surrounded the statue began pelting stones on them.
Police said they have closed the busy highway near which the statue is located. They could not say who was responsible for the garland.
PTI said Manohar Joshi, chief minister of Maharashtra state where Bombay is located, would make a statement on the incident later on Friday in the local legislature.
Ambedkar, known as the father of India's constitution, is treated like a god by the lower social classes in India's rigid Hindu caste society.
